title: What these tools actually are
takeaway: Claude Code and OpenCode are not chatbots; they take action on your computer. Stop asking questions, start giving instructions.

title: Plan mode (the most underused feature)
takeaway: Flip the AI into a look-but-do-not-touch state so it writes a plan you can correct before any work happens. Use it for tasks longer than 10 minutes.

title: Permissions discipline
takeaway: Keep the AI on a short leash at first, reading every permission request, and only auto-approve safe actions (read, tests, git status) as trust is earned.

title: Match the model to the task
takeaway: Plan with your strongest model and execute with a cheap one; the biggest cost saving with zero quality loss.

title: Context rot is real
takeaway: Conversations silently degrade as they grow; keep sessions short and focused and reset when you pass roughly half the window.

title: /clear and /compact
takeaway: /clear wipes for a brand-new task, /compact shrinks the current one; compact at task boundaries and file the facts first.

title: Resume sessions
takeaway: Conversations auto-save so you can pick up later and undo mistakes, but treat undo as a safety net, never a substitute for git.

title: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md done well
takeaway: The rules file is permanent project instructions the AI reads every turn; keep it short and add a line only when a mistake earns it.

title: Commands and skills
takeaway: A skill or command is a saved, reusable instruction file; save anything you find yourself typing more than twice.

title: Hooks and plugins
takeaway: Automatic rules that run every time with no model judgment — turning your setup into a verification loop: attempt, check, fix, repeat.

title: Subagents
takeaway: An isolated agent with its own context window does the heavy reading in private and returns only a summary; delegate info-heavy tasks.

title: MCP, used honestly
takeaway: Model Context Protocol connects the AI to live services (Slack, GitHub, databases); connect only what you need, every server costs tokens.

title: Terminal, IDE, or desktop?
takeaway: Start in the terminal so you can see which files the model reads and which commands it runs; every fancier interface is a thin wrapper.

title: Build a personal context library, slowly
takeaway: Put shared style and conventions in your home config and add items one at a time only when real problems demand them.

title: Memory beyond the basics
takeaway: Keep a notes/ folder or memory server with absolute dates and decisions, written for a reader who knows nothing — because that reader is always a future session.
